articles.title: Appellate Courts Must Give Independent Reasons, Can't Simply Overturn Trial Court Verdict As Erroneous: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that first appellate courts in India cannot overturn trial court verdicts simply by labeling them as erroneous. Instead, they must independently evaluate evidence and provide their own reasoning. The Court emphasized that appellate courts should act as mentors to subordinate courts rather than adopting a superior stance. The ruling was delivered by a Bench of Justice Sanjay Karol and Justice Aravind Kumar.
articles.raw_summary: The Supreme Court has held that a first appellate court cannot overturn a trial court's judgment merely by declaring it erroneous without independently evaluating the evidence and recording its own reasons. Stressing the duty cast upon appellate courts while reversing findings of fact, the Court observed that they must act as "a friend, philosopher and a guide" to subordinate courts rather than adopting a superior approach of merely pointing out errors. articles.title: Article 227 cannot be invoked to challenge Arbitral Tribunal’s rejection of Section 16 application; Remedy lies under Section 34 after final award: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that Article 227 of the Constitution cannot be used to challenge an arbitral tribunal's rejection of a Section 16 application. The Court emphasized minimal judicial interference in arbitral proceedings and stated that remedies must be sought under Section 34 only after a final award is issued. The ruling reinforces the legislative policy of limiting judicial intervention in arbitration.

articles.title: Is Application For Probate Of Will Time-Barred If Not Filed Within 3 Years Of Testator's Death? Supreme Court Answers
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the application for probate of a Will is not necessarily time-barred if filed within three years of the testator's death. The Court clarified that the right to apply for probate arises only when necessary, such as when someone challenges the validity of the Will. Justice Sanjay observed, “The right to apply would therefore accrue from the date that it becomes necessary to apply. This obviously need not be within three years from the death of the testator.”
articles.raw_summary: The Supreme Court has held the probate of Will need not be necessarily filed within three years of the testator's death.
